sections.heading: 1. Combustion
points: **Combustion** = a chemical process in which a substance reacts with **oxygen** to give **heat (and usually light)**.
The substance that burns is a **combustible substance / fuel**.

sub: A **fuel** (combustible substance), **air (oxygen)**, and reaching the **ignition temperature** (the lowest temperature at which a substance catches fire).

sections.heading: 2. Types of Combustion
points: **Rapid combustion** — burns quickly with heat and light (e.g. gas stove).
**Spontaneous combustion** — catches fire on its own without a flame (e.g. phosphorus, forest fires).
**Explosion** — sudden reaction producing heat, light, sound and gas (e.g. crackers).
Substances with a **low ignition temperature** (like petrol) are **inflammable/dangerous**.

sections.heading: 3. Flame and its Zones
points: Substances that **vaporise** during burning give a **flame** (e.g. wax, kerosene).

points.text: A candle flame has three zones:
sub: **Innermost (dark) zone** — unburnt wax vapour, no combustion (coolest).
**Middle (yellow, luminous) zone** — partial combustion (bright, gives light).

sections.heading: 4. Fuels and Fire Control
points: A **good fuel** is cheap, readily available, burns easily, has a **high calorific value** and low pollution.
**Calorific value** = heat produced by burning 1 kg of a fuel (unit: **kilojoule per kg**). **Hydrogen** has the highest.

**Fire control** removes one of the three requirements: **water** (cools below ignition temperature — not for oil/electrical fires); **CO₂** (cuts off oxygen — best for oil/electrical fires); a **fire extinguisher**.
Incomplete combustion produces **carbon monoxide (poisonous)**; burning fuels causes **air pollution and global warming (CO₂)**.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Combustion = burning in oxygen giving heat & light; needs fuel + air + ignition temperature.
Types: rapid, spontaneous, explosion; low ignition temperature = inflammable.
Flame zones: dark (unburnt, coolest) → yellow (luminous) → blue (complete combustion, hottest).
Calorific value = heat per kg (kJ/kg); hydrogen is highest.
Fire control: water (cools) — not for oil/electrical; CO₂ cuts off oxygen (best for oil/electrical).

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Three conditions** for combustion: fuel, air/oxygen, and reaching the **ignition temperature**.
The **outermost (blue) zone** of a flame is the **hottest**; the innermost dark zone is coolest.
**Water must NOT be used** on oil or electrical fires; use **CO₂**.
**Ignition temperature** = lowest temperature at which a substance catches fire.
